_README: mg/day -> tablets / liquid display rules (clinician summary only; never changes the decision). Encodes Dr. Barbour's answers in kristen/dose_to_tablet_conversion_scenarios.xlsx, sheet 'Flags & clarifications', column G (flags #1-#10), plus her 2026-10-25 answers on form and tablet strength (#61, #62, #66). Tablet/liquid strengths come from data/asm_rules.json formulations_rxnorm. verified:true.

window._doc: Flag #1: acceptable dose = target -10% .. +30%, applied to the TOTAL daily dose ('Try with total dose, and then lets look at increment').

rounding._doc: Flag #2 'Bias up'. Her worked example (flags #3/#4: 30 kg, levetiracetam 250 mg tablets, 1000 -> 1300 mg/day gives 500 mg morning + 750 mg night = 1250, -3.8%, not 1500) picks the CLOSEST dose, so: closest total first, ties go up. Then whole tablets over halves, even over uneven, fewest tablets. Flag #4 '+25% is acceptable' at the goal. Flag #5 lamotrigine 'Round up' (no lamotrigine exception). Flag #6: OK to round above the usual effective max; the absolute max is never crossed (NON_NEGOTIABLE_RULES #2, flag #10).

age_form_rule._doc: Dr. Barbour 2026-10-25 (#61 RESOLVED): stay with the form the family already uses (tablets stay tablets, liquid stays liquid). The age cutoff (older than 10 y = tablets, 10 and under = liquid) is used ONLY when the current form is not known - i.e. when simulating patient cases. In practice a child may use tablets earlier. If the preferred form has no usable product, the other form is shown with a note.

strength_choice._doc: Dr. Barbour 2026-10-25 (#62/#66 RESOLVED): there is no standard tablet strength. For each step, the strength is the one that fits that dose best with the fewest tablets in total; one strength per step. The strength may change between steps (e.g. 1 x 750 mg twice a day -> 2 x 500 mg twice a day). Ranking: closest total to the ladder dose (ties go up), then fewest half tablets, then fewest tablets, then the child's current strength.

form_continuity._doc: Flag #3: 'If they are on tablets, continue tablets. If they are on liquid, continue liquid.' Reconfirmed by Dr. Barbour 2026-10-25 (#61): stay consistent with what the family already uses.

uneven_dosing._doc: Flag #7: 'Allow uneven dosing for all the medications'. Flag #3 example: 1 tablet morning, 2 tablets night. Split kept within the 30/70 .. 40/60 range from the decision-table footnote; the larger dose goes at night (her examples).

half_tablets._doc: Flag #3: '1/2 tablets if needed as a first step (ending on an even dose though)'. Halves only on a non-final climb step, only for plain (scored-type) tablets, never ER/DR (flag #9). Dr. Barbour 2026-10-25 (#60): capsules can never be split, so the earlier valproate 500 mg / zonisamide 50 mg half-unit override is removed; use the products available in practice (she is separating tablets and capsules in her sheet).

combine_steps._doc: Flag #3: 'You can also try doing both dose step increases at once, instead of breaking it up into two steps.' Offered when a climb step has no tablet option in the window.

extended_release._doc: Flag #9: 'ER/DR cannot be split in half. If needed, you can switch to IR and having them go back to twice a day dosing.' ER (once-daily) products are not used for the step grid.
extended_release.fallback: switch to immediate-release, twice a day

liquid_default_mg_per_ml._doc: Flag #8: valproate liquid default 50 mg/mL ('I agree with your default').

max_units_per_dose._doc: Search bound for listing options (usability, not a clinical value): combinations of more tablets than this per dose are not listed. Dr. Barbour 2026-10-25 (#65): settings to follow her initiation-rule examples (file not yet received).

liquid_rounding._doc: Dr. Barbour 2026-10-25: the family message and the doctor's summary show only the decided (measurable) dose, never the exact ladder value (e.g. 1112.14 mg/day or 1.94 mL). Liquid doses are rounded to this step per dose; the mg/day shown is what that volume gives. Stays inside the -10%/+30% window, above the previous dose, never above the absolute max. The 0.1 mL step is my DRAFT proposal - FLAG FOR DR. BARBOUR to confirm.
